Furthermore, the tumor exhibits a very sharp transition zone on FLAIR (median thickness 0.75 mm), which is characteristic of IDH-wildtype gliomas, as opposed to the more infiltrative, ill-defined borders of IDH-mutant astrocytomas. The only weakly contradicting feature is the qualitative description of 'Mild' enhancement, but the quantitative data (volume, thick margin) are more compelling. The collective evidence strongly supports an IDH-wildtype status.

The presence of a non-enhancing central core, representing radiological necrosis (NCR Volume of 1.43 mL), is a key imaging feature corresponding to the histopathological hallmark of a WHO Grade 4 glioma. This is further supported by the presence of a thick ('>3mm') rim of contrast enhancement. While Grade 3 tumors can enhance, the combination of enhancement and central necrosis is, by definition, characteristic of a Grade 4 tumor. The patient's age (52) is also within the typical range for a primary glioblastoma (Grade 4).
